transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Please avoid strenuous activity and heavy lifting for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful to know. My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it’s mild and things just seem brighter than you’re used to, wear sunglasses when you go outside. But significant pain in bright light or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if the eye is also red and painful, and we may need to check it further. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's reassuring. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting more blurry, we may need to check it. Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you. I have no more questions.

verdict.label: pass
